items.title: An open modal inside nested shadow roots hides the whole accessibility tree
items.evidence: DialogContent.vue:196 (and SheetContent.vue:308) renders reka's modal content, which calls useHideOthers on the content element (node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Dialog/DialogContentModal.js:52-53, glass's installed reka 2.10.1; hassio reports the same call on 2.11.0; dist/shared/useHideOthers.js:13-20). aria-hidden 1.2.6's unwrapHost returns the innermost shadow host only (node_modules/aria-hidden/dist/es2015/index.js:12-14). correctTargets logs 'not contained inside' and drops it (:15-28), and hideOthers then marks every other child of body hidden (:124-134, the walk at :54-89). Booked as the FIRST row of 11.1.2's accessibility seat: docs/tranches/BL/driver/glass-11.1.1-scope.md:103 (O-358, the same repro from hassio's r11 GLASS-MAP.md). INBOUND still shows O-358 as 11.1.1 because that file was the 11.1.1 scope then (its header, line 1). Not built: `git grep hideOthers` finds nothing in src on master or on release/11.1.1. The wider shadow-root focus work is PLAN.md:224 (W-K.1).
items.row: LF-38 (hassio, round 13, sent first). With a modal Dialog or Sheet open inside Home Assistant's nested shadow roots, the accessibility tree is empty, the sheet included. reka's modal content calls aria-hidden's hideOthers. That call unwraps one shadow host, finds it outside body, and hides every other child of body, `<home-assistant>` among them. Confirmed in source. This is the same fault as O-358, already the first accessibility row of 11.1.2. The cure there: a harness page with two nested shadow roots; only what lies outside the content is hidden, at every shadow level; the open sheet is found by role in both engines. hassio's recording test, which turns green on the fix, is a second witness. The cards keep their sheets modal and keep the admin entry outside sheets until then.
items.reply: This is already booked as the first accessibility fix in 11.1.2. An open Dialog or Sheet will hide only what lies outside it, across every shadow root, so a screen reader reads the sheet and nothing behind it, and your recording test should turn green on that release.

items.title: A Select inside a Sheet on a phone opens a second sheet
items.evidence: SelectContent.vue:55-65 opens the listbox as a bottom sheet whenever the viewport is under 30rem. useSheetWidth (src/components/_shared/overlay/sheet-width.ts:13-39) reads only the viewport and knows nothing of an enclosing Sheet. release/11.1.1 keeps that form (SelectContent.vue:61-72 there). 11.1.1 only holds the form through the exit and makes it firm glass (ca17dd857). Booked: glass-11.1.1-scope.md:163 (O-399, atlas, 11.1.2): the list does not cover the sheet it lives in with a second sheet, and the surface names the field it sets; 'Rule the form first (a sheet over a sheet, a popover inside it, or the list in place)'. INBOUND O-399 states the same fault.
items.row: LF-40 (hassio). On a phone, a Select inside a device Sheet (a fan's preset, a light's effect) opens its listbox as a second sheet, with its own scrim and detents, for a choice of three words. SelectContent picks the sheet form from the viewport width alone (under 30rem) and ignores the surface it sits in. This is the same fault as O-399 (atlas), booked for 11.1.2, which rules the form first. hassio's wish, the anchored list or the list in place in the sheet's body, is recorded beside atlas's for that ruling. The dashboard keeps its own choice line until then.
items.reply: This is booked for 11.1.2, together with the same report from another site. A Select opened inside a sheet will stop stacking a second sheet over it: it will open as an anchored list or in place, and it will name the field it sets.

items.title: An open glass Dialog draws two backdrop lenses, and its veil bands on a phone
items.evidence: DialogContent.vue:195 passes `veil` to ModalOverlay and is its only passer (SheetContent.vue:307 passes none). ModalOverlay.vue:87 mounts span.glass-focus-veil. focus-veil.css:72-73 gives it backdrop-filter: blur(var(--glass-focus-veil-blur)) saturate(var(--glass-saturate)), masked at :82-145 around a fixed core: src/styles/tokens/glass.css:112-116 (blur 20 px, core 13rem by 13rem, bloom 7rem, dim a 50 % mix of --glass-plate-overlay). The plate is .glass-floating (DialogContent.vue:183; ladder.css:138, tokens/glass.css:91). Setting --glass-focus-veil-blur to 0 still leaves blur(0) saturate(1.5), a live backdrop filter, so no declared opt-out exists. Unchanged on release/11.1.1 (no diff to focus-veil.css, ModalOverlay.vue or tokens/glass.css). Related 11.1.2 bookings: INBOUND O-390(e) names the light veil's dark pool under the plate (ModalOverlay.vue:20-24, tokens/glass.css:116). Scope :130's (e) line names only the ink, so the 11.1.2 seat must carry the pool from the INBOUND row. O-353 seat B: the veil does not repaint through its open (scope :99). O-381(a): a scrim prop on the dialog family, booked 11.1.2, though by this release rule a new prop is a minor.
items.row: LF-15 (hassio, with the owner's P10 'these modals should be more glassy'). An open glass Dialog draws two backdrop lenses: its plate and the centred focus veil. A page with the dock therefore holds three. On a 390 phone in light, the veil's fixed 13rem core and 7rem bloom leave a sharp band and a dark smeared band on one screen; dark reads well. Read: only DialogContent passes the veil, and the veil's blur token cannot remove its lens. The light phone band is O-390(e)'s dark pool, booked for 11.1.2. The 11.1.2 seat takes the pool from INBOUND O-390(e), since the scope's (e) line names only the ink. The repaint is O-353's, also 11.1.2. New, 11.3.0: a declared way to keep the veil's dim and mask without its backdrop filter (one lens per open dialog), and a stated lens count in the dialog's docs. It may ride the dialog family's scrim prop (O-381(a)). Dropping the veil's frost by default is the owner's choice and is not taken: P10 asks for more glass.
items.reply: In 11.1.2 the light dialog's veil stops leaving a dark, smeared pool around the plate. In 11.3.0 a dialog gets a way to keep the veil's dim without its own blur, so an open dialog costs one lens, and the docs will state that cost.

items.title: A detented Sheet's drag cannot be kept to its grip, and the sheet's edges
items.evidence: Drag: detents/use.ts:62 (DRAG_HANDLES: grip or header) and :170-189 (the body drags when scrollIsAtLeadingEdge, :94-101). Pointer capture is taken at pointerdown (:189), before the axis is known. No prop narrows it (SheetContentProps, SheetContent.vue:27-48). release/11.1.1 keeps the same path (use.ts:254-278 there). Dismiss: SheetContent has no `dismiss` (SheetContent.vue:27-48; its comment at :334-338 says a sheet's dismissal is always free), while Dialog has one (DialogContent.vue:31, :40, :156-161). Refused fling: a fling to 0 calls requestClose() and then settle(0) whatever the root answers (master use.ts:220-223; release/11.1.1 use.ts:308-312 calls leave()). With the root still open, the content stays mounted (SheetContent.vue:176-178) and modal at size 0. Safe area: sheet/styles.css:569-572 pads with --space-family only; no env(safe-area-inset-*) appears in sheet or dialog on either tree. Corners: the four side rules (sheet/styles.css:574-589) each set two corner longhands under :where(), at 0,0,0. SheetContent.vue:113 composes .glass-floating, whose border-radius: var(--radius-ctx) (ladder.css:134, 0,1,0, same layer) sets all four at the 24 the sheet publishes (SheetContent.vue:295). So every side, not only the bottom, rounds its anchored corners: the same cascade race as LF-10. Hover: material.css:323-335 lifts .glass-floating:hover::before with no (hover: hover) gate. dialog/styles.css:129-134 already gates the close's hover that way. bl/specular/proto (V-A 14583ba7b, tip 3795843de; scope :115, ruled 11.1.2 in INBOUND O-367a) removes the ::before from .glass-floating. On its tip, material.css:264 .glass-specular-track:hover::before is the only hover catch-light left.
items.row: LF-16 (hassio). Seven points on the detented Sheet. Drag: it starts from the grip, the header, or a body at its top, and a host inside another app cannot keep it to the grip. Edge: a press at the screen's edge takes pointer capture. Dismiss: a sheet has no dismiss axis. Plate: it has no safe-area pad, it rounds its anchored corners, and it keeps its hover catch-light lit after a touch. All confirmed in source. 11.1.2, as defects with no new API: (1) every side's anchored corners go square, one change with LF-10, the side rules winning over the floating rung's --radius-ctx; (2) the bottom safe area joins the bottom sheet's own padding, and the CHANGELOG tells hosts that pad for the home bar themselves to drop it; (3) the catch-light leaves the plate through the specular change already booked for 11.1.2; if that change slips, a (hover: hover) gate on the rung's hover is the patch cure alone; (4) a fling to 0 that the root refuses springs back to the rung it left, not resting invisible, still open and modal. 11.3.0, as new props: a drag region (grip, chrome or all; today's 'all' the default); an edge inset where a press never starts a drag; and Dialog's dismiss axis on SheetContent. For the edge inset, read first whether taking capture on the first vertical move, not at pointerdown, frees the host's swipe. If it does, that change needs no prop and goes to 11.1.2 as a defect cure, and the inset is not built. Point 7, the tall head, asks nothing.
items.reply: 11.1.2 squares a sheet's corners where it meets the screen edge and adds the home-bar safe area to the bottom sheet's padding, so you can drop your own pad then. It also clears the highlight a touch leaves lit. A pull your app refuses will spring back to where it came from. 11.3.0 adds a drag-region setting (grip only, for one), an edge inset where a press never starts a drag, and the same dismiss setting the dialog has.

items.title: The light glass Dialog paints a mid-brown plate its words do not read on
items.evidence: dialog/styles.css:76-80 records the painted light plate at 3.295:1 against even --foreground. The plate ink is --glass-veil-ink oklch(0.28 0.035 70) at the dialog rung (src/styles/tokens/glass.css:34, :137, :174; DialogContent.vue:171-172). The scrim is hsl(24 10% 10%) at 50 % (src/styles/tokens/glass-fx.css:213-214). The veil's dim mixes --glass-plate-overlay (tokens/glass.css:116, :169). The floating rung points --muted-foreground at --on-glass-muted (ladder.css:199-209), which is hsl(30 26% 35%) = rgb(112 89 66) (tokens/on-glass-fg.css:35). The labelled Separator's word inks with it (Separator.vue:80, rule at :172-174). Arithmetic on hassio's measured plate rgb(118 105 86) (relative luminance 0.146): --foreground gives 3.2:1, and even pure black only 3.9:1. So no ink change reaches 4.5:1, and the painted plate itself must lighten. None of these files changed on release/11.1.1. Booked: INBOUND O-390(e), 'Light Dialog and Sheet: text 3.2 to 3.5:1 ... the focus veil also paints a dark pool', and scope :130 (e), 'light Dialog, Sheet and menu ink to 4.5:1 for words'. Precedent: the firm plate 11.1.1 built for the phone Select (release/11.1.1 surface-axis.css:99, ca17dd857).
items.row: LF-17 (hassio, with P10 and LF-13). Over a light page, the light glass Dialog paints a mid-brown plate, about rgb(118 105 86). On it --foreground reads 3.2:1, the muted rung 1.2:1, and the labelled Separator's word 1.18:1. The dashboard runs the solid plate in light until this ships. Read: the library records the same 3.295:1 in dialog/styles.css, and the cards set none of these tokens. This is the same fault as O-390(e), booked for 11.1.2. This row adds witness lines to it: --foreground and every --muted-foreground line, the Separator's word included, at 4.5:1 on the light dialog over a light page, with the measured figures in the CHANGELOG. Even pure black reads only 3.9:1 on this plate, so the painted plate must lighten: the plate frosting toward the card, as 11.1.1's firm plate does for a phone Select, or the light scrim dimming less. That also serves P10.
items.reply: This is booked for 11.1.2. The light glass dialog's plate lifts so that its words and muted lines, the labelled separator's word included, read at 4.5:1 over a light page, with the measured figures in the changelog. You can then drop the solid plate in light.

items.title: The Dialog draws the card's 16 corner, not the room's 24 (paired with LF-27)
items.evidence: dialog/styles.css:21-22 sets border-radius: var(--radius-3xl) under :where() (0,0,0); its comment at :14-19 and radius.css:33-45 rule the plate a room at 24. DialogContent.vue:183 composes .glass-floating, whose border-radius: var(--radius-ctx) (ladder.css:124, :134; same components layer, 0,1,0) wins. DialogContent.vue:171-175 publishes no --radius-ctx, so the plate reads the root's --radius-card (radius.css:224, then :138), 16. SheetContent.vue:295-296 publishes --radius-ctx: var(--radius-3xl) and --radius-inset: var(--space-family). Unchanged on release/11.1.1: its DialogContent and dialog/styles.css diffs touch no radius. Placed in 11.1.2 by INBOUND O-377a, LF-10's own first reading. Not a separate booking: this is the same ask, re-sent as a pair. Effects of the relay cure, for the witness and CHANGELOG: CommandDialog composes DialogContent (CommandDialog.vue:74) and moves to 24 with it. The glass rungs read var(--radius-ctx) raw (ladder.css:64, :90, :106, :134, :153), so a bare glass plate nested in a dialog draws 24, as one inside a Sheet does today. A nested Card keeps 16, since card/styles.css:39 loads after glass.css (styles/index.css:202, :209). Only configurator/styles.css:152 and tabs/styles/segmented.css:112 read the derived corner max(floor, ctx − inset).
items.row: LF-10, re-placed with LF-27, which hassio sends as a pair: the dialog and the card at the room rung. LF-10 stays an 11.1.2 defect, as O-377a placed it: the source states 24 and a cascade race paints 16. DialogContent publishes the room corner and its pad through the relay, as SheetContent does (--radius-ctx: var(--radius-3xl), --radius-inset: var(--space-family)). The plate then draws 24, and a nested element that reads the relay derives a concentric corner from it. CommandDialog moves to 24 with it, and a bare glass plate nested in a dialog draws 24, as it does in a Sheet. Both are named in the witness and the CHANGELOG. Every sheet side's anchored corners (LF-16, point 6) go square in the same release, the side rules winning over the rung. LF-27 is a new Card size, a minor, and waits for 11.3.0. The pair therefore lands in two steps, and the Card size reuses this relay.
items.reply: 11.1.2 gives the dialog the 24 px corner the radius rules promise, published the way the sheet publishes its corner, so rows of your own inside it can take a matching inner corner. The command palette takes the same corner. The room-sized Card follows in 11.3.0.

items.title: A Card at the room rung
items.evidence: card/styles.css:35-41: .card has corner --radius-card (16) and --card-pad --space-body (12). card/styles.css:43-47: sm is one rung down (pad 8, gaps 4 and 8) with the corner unchanged. Card.vue:8: CardSize is 'sm' | 'md'. radius.css:33-45 sets the room role at --radius-3xl (24) with r − pad = 4 and binds it to dialog, sheet and drawer by name. Card publishes no relay (no --radius-ctx or --radius-inset in src/components/card). The publishers are SheetContent.vue:295-296, Configurator.vue:334-335, overlay-plate.css:64-65 and :137-138, and tabs/styles/segmented.css:101-102. Only configurator/styles.css:152 and segmented.css:112 read the derived corner. A nested Card keeps its own 16 (card/styles.css:39), and a bare glass rung reads --radius-ctx raw (ladder.css:64, :90, :106). release/11.1.1 adds only a reduced-motion press rule to card/styles.css. 11.2.0 touches the dock only (RULINGS-7.md:394-465), so this is not small work on a part 11.2.0 already touches.
items.row: LF-27 (hassio, with the owner's 'more rounded' of 2026-11-19 and P20). The ask: a Card at the room rung, with the 24 corner and the 20 pad its pairing law gives, publishing --radius-ctx and --radius-inset so a nested row draws max(floor, 24 − 20). Read: Card has only sm and md, neither changes the corner, and Card publishes no relay at all. A new size value is a minor, so this lands in 11.3.0, after LF-10's dialog relay (11.1.2), which it reuses. The 11.3.0 build names the size and adds a line to radius.css saying a Card may take the room rung, which the canon now binds to dialog, sheet and drawer by name. Its witness reads a nested row that uses the derivation. A bare glass plate inside reads the relay's corner raw, as inside a Sheet. The dashboard's dated rule stays until then.
items.reply: A room-sized Card (24 px corner, 20 px pad, publishing its corner so rows inside sit concentric) is a new size, so it comes in 11.3.0. Keep your dated rule until then.

items.title: The Dialog's and Sheet's close glyph is a fixed size no token reaches
items.evidence: DialogContent.vue:221-235 (class at :223) and SheetContent.vue:342-356 (class at :344) draw the close glyph with class w-4 h-4 (Tailwind spacing, 1rem). release/11.1.1 has the same at DialogContent.vue:263 and SheetContent.vue:394. dialog/styles.css:97 states the designed size: 'glyph 16'. So at a 16 px root the glyph is as designed, and the 14 px under Home Assistant's 14 px root is LF-1 (INBOUND O-377a), whose px base size moved to 12.0.0 (RULINGS-7.md:562). What is missing is a hook. Button sizes an unsized svg from --ui-glyph (button/styles.css:113-115; tokens/sizing.css:53, 1rem × --ui-scale). On a coarse pointer --ui-scale is 1.5 (tokens/light-dark.css:17-19), so reading that token makes the ✕ 24 px on every touch screen for every consumer. That is a visible change to a default, never a patch. Glass's --icon-md is 1rem and its 20 is --icon-lg (tokens/sizing.css:92-93). Booked beside it: O-341 at scope :90 makes the close a round icon button on the IconButton recipe (11.1.2). That rework must keep the 16 px glyph on every pointer so it does not bring this change early.
items.row: LF-35 (hassio, the owner's P18: icons larger than 14 px). The close glyph on Dialog and Sheet is a fixed w-4 h-4. That is 14 px under Home Assistant's 14 px root, and no token or slot reaches it. Read: 16 px is the designed size (dialog/styles.css says so), and the 14 px is LF-1's root-size fault, now 12.0.0. The ask is a hook, so this is a feature, not a defect. In 11.3.0 the close glyph reads --ui-glyph, the token Button's glyphs read. It stays 16 at a 16 px root on a fine pointer, a host raises it with the token it already uses for button glyphs, and on a coarse pointer it grows with the comfort scale, as every button glyph does; the release notes say so. That coarse growth is a change every consumer sees, which is why this is not 11.1.2. O-341's close rework in 11.1.2 keeps the glyph at 16 on every pointer. A close-only token or a close slot would be further new API, taken only if the shared token proves too broad.
items.reply: The close button's ✕ is drawn at 16 px by design. It reads 14 px inside Home Assistant because of the page's root size, which is planned for 12.0.0. Setting its size yourself is new, so it comes in 11.3.0: the ✕ will take its size from the same token as button icons, so that one token can raise it to 20 px, and on touch screens it will grow with the other icons.

changed: LF-35: moved from glass defect / 11.1.2 to glass feature / 11.3.0. The 16 px glyph is as designed (dialog/styles.css:97) and the 14 px is LF-1 (12.0.0), so the ask is a hook. Reading --ui-glyph makes the close glyph 24 px on every touch screen (tokens/light-dark.css:17-19), and a look change is never a patch. RULINGS-7 line corrected from 564 to 562.

LF-10: dedupe_of O-377a removed. O-377a is LF-10's own first reading, not a separate booking, and the verdict is a defect. Corrected the claim that a nested plate derives its corner from the relay: only configurator/styles.css:152 and segmented.css:112 derive; the glass rungs read --radius-ctx raw (ladder.css:64, :90, :106, :134, :153). Added the cure's visible effects for the witness and CHANGELOG: CommandDialog moves to 24 (CommandDialog.vue:74); a nested Card keeps 16 (card/styles.css:39, loaded after glass.css).

Added a standalone (hover: hover) gate as the 11.1.2 cure if the specular change slips (precedent dialog/styles.css:129-134).
